'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Religion in the United Arab Emirates]]
**The [[Emirate of Dubai]] in the [[United Arab Emirates]] reopens its [[Catholic Church in the United Arab Emirates|Catholic churches]], including [[St. Mary's Catholic Church, Dubai|St. Mary's]] and [[St. Francis of Assisi Catholic Church, Jebel Ali|St. Francis of Assisi]] in [[Jebel Ali]], after three months of closure amidst the Iran war. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260701-sony-says-to-stop-releasing-playstation-games-on-discs (AFP via France 24)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
***The [[International Transport Workers' Federation]] and the Joint Negotiating Group of [[Maritime shipping|shipping]] owners announce they will continue to designate the [[Strait of Hormuz]] as a warzone, which doubles the pay of mariners there and gives them other benefits. [https://aje.news/313ayw?update=4722059 (Al Jazeera)]
**[[2026 Iran war fuel crisis]]
***[[Saudi Aramco]] and [[Algeria]]n oil company [[Sonatrach]] announce that they will cut prices for [[liquefied petroleum gas]] for July, with Saudi Aramco reducing it between 24% and 27% and Sonatrach reducing it between 2% and 10%. [https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/saudi-aramco-sonatrach-cut-lpg-prices-july-2026-07-01/ (Reuters)]
*[[Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Ukraine]] approves a mechanism for exporting [[Defense industry of Ukraine|domestically produced weapons]] and [[Military technology|military technologies]] to raise funds for [[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|its defense effort]] against [[Russia]] and attract [[Economy of Ukraine|foreign investment]], while requiring that the [[Ukrainian military]]'s supply needs remain the priority. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/kyiv-launches-mechanism-allowing-allies-to-buy-ukrainian-weapons (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]
*[[The Philippines and the World Bank]]
**The [[World Bank]] classifies the [[Philippines]] as an [[Developing country|upper-middle-income]] economy, up from lower-middle-income status, after its per capita [[gross national income]] exceeds the [[fiscal year]] 2026 threshold of [[US$]]4,496 to $13,935. [https://www.agenzianova.com/en/news/World-Bank-promotes-Philippines-to-upper-middle-income-country/ (Agenzia Nova)]
*[[United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement]]
**[[United States Trade Representative|U.S. trade representative]] [[Jamieson Greer]] says that the [[United States]] will not renew the USMCA [[trade agreement]] signed during [[President of the United States|president]] [[Donald Trump]]'s [[First presidency of Donald Trump|first term]]. The U.S. will conduct annual reviews of the trade agreement and will conduct negotiations and amendments to it. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/cusma-usmca-trump-extension-renewal-9.7255204 (CBC News)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/business/economy/trump-usmca-renewal-tariffs-trade-rcna352594 (NBC News)] [https://mexiconewsdaily.com/business/us-mexico-not-renew-usmca/ (Mexico News Daily)]
